references.text: Jesus himself stood among the disciples after the resurrection. In [ref:Luk 24:36|Luke 24:36], Jesus suddenly appears to the eleven, just as he here suddenly joins the two on the road to Emmaus.

[ref:Mark 16:12|Mark 16:12] is a parallel account that mentions that Jesus appeared "in another form" to two of the disciples while they were walking in the countryside – a reference to the same event on the road to Emmaus.
In [ref:Joh 20:14|John 20:14], Mary Magdalene did not recognize the risen Jesus, similarly to how the travelers on the road to Emmaus did not recognize him when he approached and walked with them.

In [ref:Joh 21:4|John 21:4], Jesus stood on the shore in the morning, but the disciples did not know it was him. A recurring pattern after the resurrection: Jesus appears, but is not immediately recognized.
[ref:Luk 24:16|Luke 24:16] explains directly why the two disciples did not recognize Jesus when he joined them: "their eyes were kept from recognizing him".

In [ref:Luk 24:28-29|Luke 24:28-29], the story continues that Jesus walked with them all the way to Emmaus, where they asked him to stay with them. He who "approached and walked with them" (v. 15) follows them all the way.

In [ref:Matt 18:20|Matthew 18:20], Jesus promises: "For where two or three are gathered in my name, there am I among them." Here this promise is literally fulfilled as Jesus joins the two who are talking about him on the road.

[ref:Luk 24:31|Luke 24:31] describes the moment when their eyes were opened and they recognized him – the decisive turning point that contrasts with the meeting in verse 15 where they did not recognize him.

In [ref:1 Mos 18:1-2|Genesis 18:1-2], the Lord appears to Abraham in the form of three men who approach him. An Old Testament parallel where God joins people on the road without them immediately understanding whom they are meeting.
